title: Build the typed API client in src/api
prompt:
Story S-04 builds the Vue 3 + TypeScript web UI for the book catalog in `frontend/`. It is a client of the existing `/api/books` endpoints of the `catalog` bounded context and uses its language: a *book* is *added* to the *catalog*, *revised* and *removed*. The backend and `backend/api/openapi.yaml` don't change.

Rules for every frontend task:
- Gate: `cd frontend && npm run typecheck && npm test` must pass; run both before you finish. `npm run typecheck` first regenerates `src/api/schema.d.ts` from the spec (openapi-typescript). That file is gitignored and must never be edited or replaced by hand-written types.
- You can't run `npm install`, so add no dependencies. If one seems needed, propose it in `.orch-proposals.json`.
- No `any` (use `unknown` and narrow) and no `v-html` anywhere in `src/`. A guard test added by S04-02 fails on either.
- Only `src/api/` calls `fetch`. Tests mock the API at the `fetch` boundary.
- Tests are `*.spec.ts` files in a `__tests__/` folder (tsconfig.vitest.json type-checks only `src/**/__tests__/*`).

This task builds the one typed API client. Work only in `frontend/src/api/` (never touch `schema.d.ts`). S04-02 builds the app shell, router and test helpers in parallel. Don't touch those, and don't use their helpers. The screens (S04-03 to S04-05) are built afterwards against the contract below, so the names and signatures are binding.

Domain rules that live here (from the story):
- The client returns either the data or a typed error `{status, message}`.
- A 400 message has the form `<field>: <reason>`, e.g. `title: must have 1 to 300 characters`. If `<field>` is one of the form's fields (`isbn`, `title`, `authors`, `publishedYear`, `language`, `pages`), the screen shows the reason at that field. Any other message goes to the top of the form. Examples of other messages: `author: must be valid UTF-8 without control characters`, `limit: must be between 1 and 100`, `invalid request body`, `invalid path parameter "id"`, `unsupported content type`.
- The two different 409s on update are told apart in one place, here. The backend's message starts with `version conflict` for a *version conflict* (`version conflict: the book was changed since it was read`); anything else is a duplicate ISBN (`a book with this ISBN already exists`).

Contract: `frontend/src/api/index.ts` (imported as `@/api`) exports exactly:
- Types, derived only from the generated schema (`import type { components, paths } from './schema'`):
  - `Book` = `components['schemas']['Book']`
  - `BookInput` = `components['schemas']['BookInput']`
  - `BookUpdate` = `components['schemas']['BookUpdate']`
  - `BookList` = `components['schemas']['BookList']`
  - `ListBooksQuery` = `NonNullable<paths['/api/books']['get']['parameters']['query']>`
  - `BookField` = `keyof BookInput` (`'isbn' | 'title' | 'authors' | 'publishedYear' | 'language' | 'pages'`)
- `PAGE_SIZE = 20`.
- `type ApiErrorKind = 'network' | 'invalid' | 'not-found' | 'duplicate-isbn' | 'version-conflict' | 'other'`.
- `interface ApiError { status: number; message: string; kind: ApiErrorKind }`. Status is 0 for a network error.
- `type ApiResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: ApiError }`.
- `listBooks(query: ListBooksQuery): Promise<ApiResult<BookList>>`: GET /api/books with the given params. Undefined params and an empty `author` are left out.
- `getBook(id: number): Promise<ApiResult<Book>>`: GET /api/books/{id}.
- `createBook(input: BookInput): Promise<ApiResult<Book>>`: POST /api/books, with the body exactly as given.
- `updateBook(id: number, input: BookUpdate): Promise<ApiResult<Book>>`: PUT /api/books/{id}, with the body exactly as given.
- `deleteBook(id: number): Promise<ApiResult<null>>`: DELETE /api/books/{id}. A 204 gives `{ ok: true, data: null }`.
- `parseFieldError(message: string): { field: BookField; reason: string } | null`. It splits at the first `: `. It returns null when the prefix is not a BookField.
- The functions never throw or reject. `kind` is set as follows:
  - fetch rejected: 'network', with status 0 and message 'Could not reach the server.'
  - 400: 'invalid'
  - 404: 'not-found'
  - 409 whose message starts with `version conflict`: 'version-conflict'
  - any other 409: 'duplicate-isbn'
  - everything else: 'other'
  `message` is the API's `error` text, or `Request failed with status <n>` when the body has none.

Implementation:
- `src/api/client.ts`: `createClient<paths>` from `openapi-fetch` 0.17. Two details matter:
  1. openapi-fetch reads `globalThis.fetch` once, when the client is created, so a test's later `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...)` would be ignored. Pass `fetch: (request: Request) => globalThis.fetch(request)`, so fetch is looked up on every call.
  2. openapi-fetch builds `new Request(baseUrl + path)`. In Vitest's jsdom environment `Request` is Node's, which rejects a bare `/api/books` ("Failed to parse URL"). Use `baseUrl: globalThis.location.origin`. Requests then go to `/api/...` on the page's own origin; in dev that is Vite, which proxies `/api` to :8000. Never hardcode a host or port.
- `src/api/errors.ts`: the error types, one classification function (e.g. `toApiError(status: number, body: unknown): ApiError`) and `parseFieldError`. The 409 distinction lives only there.
- `src/api/books.ts`: the five functions. `index.ts` re-exports the contract.
- Base every decision on `response.status`/`response.ok`, not on whether openapi-fetch returned `error`. For empty bodies (a 204, or an error with Content-Length 0) it returns neither `data` nor `error`.
- Error bodies: if the body is an object with a string `error`, that is the message. Otherwise (empty, text from a proxy, unexpected JSON) use `Request failed with status <status>`.
- Wrap each call in try/catch. A rejected fetch becomes the network error. An unhandled rejection would fail the tests of every screen.
- `ApiError`, `ApiErrorKind` and `ApiResult` are the client's own types, which is fine. Write no interfaces for API shapes.

Tests go in `src/api/__tests__/*.spec.ts`. Stub fetch with `vi.stubGlobal('fetch', vi.fn(...))` returning real `Response` objects, and call `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in `afterEach`. Read method, path, query and JSON body from the `Request` the stub receives.
- listBooks:
  - `{ author: 'Martin Fowler', offset: 0, limit: 20 }` sends GET `/api/books` with author 'Martin Fowler', offset '0' and limit '20' (check them with `new URL(req.url).searchParams`).
  - `{ offset: 20, limit: 20 }` and `{ author: '', offset: 0 }` send no author.
  - A success gives `{ ok: true, data }`.
- getBook(7) sends GET `/api/books/7`.
- createBook sends POST with the exact body; `{isbn, title, authors}` stays without optional keys.
- updateBook(7, ...) sends PUT `/api/books/7` with `version`.
- deleteBook(7): a 204 gives `{ ok: true, data: null }`.
- Errors:
  - 400 `title: must have 1 to 300 characters` gives `{ status: 400, kind: 'invalid', message }`.
  - 404 gives 'not-found', also with an empty body.
  - 409 `version conflict: the book was changed since it was read` gives 'version-conflict'.
  - 409 `a book with this ISBN already exists` gives 'duplicate-isbn'.
  - 500 `internal server error` gives 'other'.
  - 502 with a text body gives the message `Request failed with status 502`.
  - fetch rejecting with `new TypeError('Failed to fetch')` gives status 0 and 'network'.
- parseFieldError:
  - Each of the six fields is recognized, e.g. `publishedYear: must be between 1450 and 2100` gives `{ field: 'publishedYear', reason: 'must be between 1450 and 2100' }`.
  - `author: ...`, `limit: ...`, `offset: ...`, `invalid request body`, `invalid path parameter "id"` and `''` give null.

title: Build the app shell, router, notice store and test helpers
prompt:
Story S-04 builds the Vue 3 + TypeScript web UI for the book catalog in `frontend/`. It is a client of the existing `/api/books` endpoints of the `catalog` bounded context and uses its language: a *book* is *added* to the *catalog*, *revised* and *removed*. The backend and `backend/api/openapi.yaml` don't change.

Rules for every frontend task:
- Gate: `cd frontend && npm run typecheck && npm test` must pass; run both before you finish. `npm run typecheck` first regenerates `src/api/schema.d.ts` from the spec (openapi-typescript). That file is gitignored and must never be edited or replaced by hand-written types.
- You can't run `npm install`, so add no dependencies. If one seems needed, propose it in `.orch-proposals.json`.
- Use `<script setup lang="ts">` SFCs, the Composition API, minimal plain scoped CSS, no UI library, and an English UI.
- No `any` (use `unknown` and narrow) and no `v-html` anywhere in `src/`. Book data is user input and is rendered only as text with `{{ }}`.
- Only `src/api/` calls `fetch`. Tests mock the API at the `fetch` boundary.
- Tests are `*.spec.ts` files in a `__tests__/` folder (tsconfig.vitest.json type-checks only `src/**/__tests__/*`).

This task builds the app shell and the shared test infrastructure. S04-01 builds the API client in `src/api/` in parallel. Don't touch `src/api/`; nothing in this task calls the API. The screens come next (S04-03 catalog page, S04-04 details, S04-05 book form). They mount through your router and helpers, so the names below are binding.

1. Remove the scaffold demo:
   - Delete `src/stores/counter.ts`.
   - Replace the "You did it!" `App.vue` and its test `src/__tests__/App.spec.ts`.
   - In `index.html`, set `<html lang="en">` and the title `Book catalog`.
   - `main.ts` keeps Pinia and the default router export.

2. Router: `frontend/src/router/index.ts` exports `routes: RouteRecordRaw[]`, `createAppRouter(history?: RouterHistory): Router` (default `createWebHistory(import.meta.env.BASE_URL)`) and, as default, the router instance. Routes:
   - `/` redirects to `{ name: 'books' }`.
   - `/books`, name `books`: `views/BookListView.vue`, no props. It reads `route.query.author` and `route.query.offset`.
   - `/books/new`, name `book-new`: `views/BookFormView.vue`, no props (add mode).
   - `/books/:id([1-9][0-9]{0,14})`, name `book`: `views/BookDetailView.vue`, with `props: (route) => ({ id: Number(route.params.id) })`.
   - `/books/:id([1-9][0-9]{0,14})/edit`, name `book-edit`: `views/BookFormView.vue`, with the same props function (edit mode).
   - `/:pathMatch(.*)*`, name `not-found`: `views/NotFoundView.vue`.
   The id pattern admits only positive integers of up to 15 digits, which are always safe integers. So `/books/abc` and `/books/0` show "Page not found".

3. Views:
   - `NotFoundView.vue`: heading "Page not found" and a RouterLink to `/books` ("Back to the catalog").
   - Placeholders, each just an `<h1>` (later tasks replace them), with exactly these props so the router props type-check:
     - `BookListView.vue`: no props, text "Catalog".
     - `BookDetailView.vue`: `defineProps<{ id: number }>()`, text "Book".
     - `BookFormView.vue`: `defineProps<{ id?: number }>()`, text "Book form".

4. Layout `App.vue`:
   - A `<header>` with the app name and a nav RouterLink "Books" to `/books`.
   - The notice region (below).
   - `<main>` with `<RouterView v-slot="{ Component, route }"><component :is="Component" :key="route.path" /></RouterView>`. A view is remounted when the path changes (`/books/7` to `/books/8`, edit to new), but not when only the query changes.

5. Notice store `src/stores/notice.ts`: `useNoticeStore`, a Pinia setup store with id 'notice', `message: string | null`, `show(text: string): void` and `clear(): void`. `App.vue`:
   - shows the message above `<main>` in a `role="status"` element with a *Dismiss* button that clears it;
   - clears it after every navigation via `useRouter().afterEach(...)`, removing the hook in `onUnmounted`.
   A view that wants a notice on the next page calls `show()` after `await router.push(...)` has resolved. S04-04 uses this for "Deleted <title>".

6. Test helpers in `frontend/src/__tests__/helpers.ts` (import as `@/__tests__/helpers`). Take the Book type from the generated schema (`import type { components } from '@/api/schema'`), because `@/api/index.ts` is written in parallel.
   - `makeBook(overrides?: Partial<Book>): Book`. Defaults: id 7, isbn '9780132350884', title 'Clean Code', authors ['Robert C. Martin'], createdAt and updatedAt '2026-01-02T03:04:05Z', version 1. No publishedYear, language or pages.
   - `jsonResponse(status: number, body: unknown): Response`, `errorResponse(status: number, message: string): Response` (body `{ error: message }`) and `noContent(): Response` (204, null body).
   - `interface RecordedRequest { method: string; url: URL; body: unknown }`. body is the parsed JSON body, or undefined if there is none.
   - `stubFetch(handler: (req: RecordedRequest) => Response | undefined | Promise<Response | undefined>): RecordedRequest[]`.
     - It replaces the global fetch with `vi.stubGlobal` and returns the live list of requests, in order.
     - Accept a `Request` or a URL plus init.
     - If the handler returns undefined, answer 501 `{ error: 'unexpected request in test: <METHOD> <path?query>' }`.
     - If the handler throws, fetch rejects with that error (`throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch')` simulates a network error).
   - `renderRoute(path: string): Promise<{ wrapper: VueWrapper; router: Router }>`. It creates a fresh Pinia (and `setActivePinia`) and `createAppRouter(createMemoryHistory())`, pushes `path`, awaits `router.isReady()`, mounts `App` with `global: { plugins: [router, pinia] }`, then awaits `flushPromises()`.
   - Call `enableAutoUnmount(afterEach)` from @vue/test-utils in the helpers module.

7. Vitest:
   - Add `unstubGlobals: true` to `test` in `vitest.config.ts`, keeping the rest.
   - Add `src/__tests__/setup.ts` as a `setupFiles` entry. Its `beforeEach` stubs `fetch` with a function that rejects with `new TypeError('unexpected network access in test: use stubFetch')`, so no test ever reaches the network. That still holds once the placeholders become real views.

8. Guard test `src/__tests__/quality.spec.ts`, for the story's Quality criteria "No `any` in `src/`" and "No `v-html` anywhere. Book data is user input and is only rendered as text."
   - Read every `.ts` and `.vue` file under `src/`, with `node:fs`/`node:path` (tsconfig.vitest has Node types) or with `import.meta.glob` and `{ query: '?raw', import: 'default', eager: true }`.
   - Skip `src/api/schema.d.ts` (generated) and the guard file itself.
   - Fail, naming the files, when one contains `v-html` or uses `any` as a type: `: any`, `as any`, `<any>`, `<any,`, `, any>`, `any[]`, `| any`.
   - English 'any' in comments or text ("Any other message", "if any") must not trip it. Add a self-check that the matcher catches each pattern and ignores such text.

Tests in `src/__tests__/App.spec.ts`, using renderRoute:
- `/` redirects to `/books`, and the header link points to `/books`.
- `/nope`, `/books/abc` and `/books/0` show "Page not found" with a link to `/books`.
- `/books/7` renders BookDetailView with the number 7 as `id` (`wrapper.findComponent(BookDetailView).props('id')`).
- `/books/7/edit` renders BookFormView with id 7, and `/books/new` renders it with id undefined.
- Notice:
  - after `show('Deleted Clean Code')` it is visible in `role="status"`;
  - *Dismiss* clears it;
  - the next navigation clears it;
  - when set after `await router.push(...)`, it is still visible on the page that push led to.
- stubFetch records method, URL and JSON body. A handler returning undefined gives a 501 with the message, and a throwing handler makes fetch reject.

title: Build the catalog page with filter and paging
prompt:
Story S-04 builds the Vue 3 + TypeScript web UI for the book catalog in `frontend/`. It is a client of the existing `/api/books` endpoints of the `catalog` bounded context and uses its language: a *book* is *added* to the *catalog*, *revised* and *removed*. The backend and `backend/api/openapi.yaml` don't change.

Rules for every frontend task:
- Gate: `cd frontend && npm run typecheck && npm test` must pass; run both before you finish. `npm run typecheck` first regenerates `src/api/schema.d.ts` from the spec. That file is gitignored and must never be edited or replaced by hand-written types.
- You can't run `npm install`, so add no dependencies. If one seems needed, propose it in `.orch-proposals.json`.
- Use `<script setup lang="ts">` SFCs, the Composition API, minimal plain scoped CSS, no UI library, and an English UI.
- No `any` (use `unknown` and narrow) and no `v-html` anywhere in `src/`; a guard test fails on either. Book data is user input and is rendered only as text with `{{ }}`.
- Only `src/api/` calls `fetch`. Tests mock the API at the `fetch` boundary.
- Tests are `*.spec.ts` files in a `__tests__/` folder.
- Every input has a `<label>`.
- While a request runs, the button that started it is disabled and the handler ignores a second call.
- Loading, empty and error states are visible. No screen stays blank or throws an unhandled error.

This task builds the *catalog page*. Replace the placeholder `src/views/BookListView.vue` (it stays prop-less) and test it in `src/views/__tests__/BookListView.spec.ts`. You may add components under `src/components/book-list/`. S04-04 (details) and S04-05 (book form) run in parallel and own their views. Don't touch other views, the router, App.vue, the store, `src/api/` or the test helpers; propose changes there instead.

API client (`@/api`, already merged; read `src/api/index.ts`):
- `listBooks(query: ListBooksQuery): Promise<ApiResult<BookList>>`, where `ListBooksQuery` is `{ author?, limit?, offset? }` from the generated spec. Undefined params and an empty author are not sent.
- `PAGE_SIZE = 20`.
- `type ApiResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: ApiError }`, where `ApiError` is `{ status, message, kind }` (status 0 for a network error) and `BookList` is `{ items: Book[], total }`.
- `Book` has id, isbn, title, authors, publishedYear?, language?, pages?, createdAt, updatedAt and version.
- The functions never throw.

Router:
- `/books` (name `books`) renders this view.
- `/books/:id` (name `book`) shows the details; `/books/new` (name `book-new`) shows the empty book form.
- App.vue keys the RouterView by `route.path`, so this view is not remounted when only the query changes.

Test helpers (`@/__tests__/helpers`):
- `makeBook(overrides?: Partial<Book>): Book`, with defaults id 7, 'Clean Code', ['Robert C. Martin'], version 1 and no optional fields.
- `jsonResponse(status, body)` and `errorResponse(status, message)`.
- `stubFetch(handler: (req: { method: string; url: URL; body: unknown }) => Response | undefined | Promise<...>)` returns the live list of recorded requests. A handler returning undefined gives a 501; a handler that throws makes fetch reject (`throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch')` is a network error).
- `renderRoute(path): Promise<{ wrapper, router }>` mounts the whole App with a memory-history router and a fresh Pinia.
- Globals are unstubbed and wrappers unmounted after each test.
- After clicks, `await flushPromises()`. Use `await vi.waitFor(() => expect(...))` where a response still has to be parsed.
- Check the URL through `router.currentRoute.value.query`. Vue Router writes spaces as `+` in `fullPath`.

Domain: the *catalog page* is the list of books, 20 per page, sorted by ID (the API sorts), optionally filtered by an exact author name. The list state (page and author filter) lives in the URL query (`/books?author=...&offset=...`), so reload, back and shared links keep it.

Behavior:
- Read the state from `route.query`:
  - `author`: a string; the first value if repeated; trimmed; empty means no filter.
  - `offset`: a non-negative integer; anything else means 0.
  Request `listBooks({ author, offset, limit: PAGE_SIZE })`. Always send `offset` and `limit`, and send `author` only when filtering.
- Watch `route.query` and reload on every change (paging, filter, back/forward).
  - React only while `route.name === 'books'`, because the watcher can fire once while navigating away.
  - Ignore responses that arrive for an outdated query.
- Table columns:
  - Title: a RouterLink to `{ name: 'book', params: { id } }`.
  - Authors: joined with ", ".
  - Published: publishedYear, or "—".
  - Language: language, or "—".
- Paging:
  - A summary `<first>–<last> of <total>` with an en dash (U+2013), e.g. "1–20 of 25" and "21–25 of 25".
  - *Previous* and *Next* buttons call `router.push({ name: 'books', query })` with the offset minus or plus 20, keeping the author. Use push, not replace, so Back works.
  - Offset 0 is left out of the URL; any other offset is in it (`offset=20`).
  - *Previous* is disabled at offset 0, *Next* when offset + items.length >= total. Both are disabled while loading.
- Author filter:
  - A form with a text input labelled "Author", a *Filter* submit button and, while a filter is active, a *Clear filter* button.
  - Submitting pushes `{ author }` without an offset (first page). Submitting an empty input, or clicking *Clear filter*, pushes `/books` with no query.
  - The input shows the filter from the URL, also after back/forward.
  - *Filter* is disabled while loading.
- *New book*: a RouterLink to `{ name: 'book-new' }`, always visible, including the empty and error states.
- States:
  - Loading: "Loading books…" with role="status".
  - Error: role="alert" with "Could not load the books: <error.message>" and a *Retry* button that requests the same query again.
  - Empty catalog (total 0, no filter): "No books yet".
  - No match for a filter: "No books by <author>" with *Clear filter*.
  - A page past the end (no items but total > 0): "No books on this page" with a link to the first page.
- Ambiguity resolved: the filter value is trimmed; matching is exact and done by the API.

Tests: mount with `renderRoute(...)`. The stubFetch handler answers `GET /api/books` from a list of books built with makeBook (e.g. 25 books with ids 1–25, some by 'Martin Fowler'). It honors `author`, `offset` and `limit` from `req.url.searchParams` and returns the matching `total`. Each acceptance criterion gets at least one test:
- Given 25 books, when I open `/books`, then I see the first 20 by ID and "1–20 of 25". *Next* shows the remaining 5 with "21–25 of 25", and the URL has `offset=20`.
- Given I'm on the first page, *Previous* is disabled. Given I'm on the last page, *Next* is disabled.
- When I filter by `Martin Fowler`, then the list is requested with `author=Martin Fowler` and `offset` 0, the URL has the filter, and clearing the filter shows all books again.
- When I open `/books?author=Martin%20Fowler&offset=20` directly, then that filter and page are loaded. Check the request, the filter input and the summary.
- Given an empty catalog, when I open `/books`, then I see "No books yet" and the *New book* button.
- Given the API fails (network error or 500), when I open `/books`, then I see an error message and a *Retry* button that reloads the list. Test both failure kinds.

Also test:
- *Previous* returns to the first page and drops `offset` from the URL.
- Each title links to `/books/<id>`: check the `href`, don't navigate.
- A 400 from the API (e.g. `invalid query parameter "author"`) is shown as an error, not a blank page.
- A filter without matches shows "No books by Martin Fowler".
- *Next* is disabled while a request is pending.

This task builds the *book form* for adding and revising. Replace the placeholder `src/views/BookFormView.vue`, keeping `defineProps<{ id?: number }>()`. Test it in `src/views/__tests__/BookFormView.add.spec.ts` and `src/views/__tests__/BookFormView.edit.spec.ts`. You may add components under `src/components/book-form/`, e.g. the authors list. API client (`@/api`, already merged; read `src/api/index.ts`):

  - `Book`: id, isbn, title, authors, publishedYear?, language?, pages?, createdAt, updatedAt, version.

  - `BookUpdate`: BookInput plus version.
  - `BookField` = `keyof BookInput`.
- Functions:
  - `getBook(id: number): Promise<ApiResult<Book>>`.
  - `createBook(input: BookInput): Promise<ApiResult<Book>>`.
  - `updateBook(id: number, input: BookUpdate): Promise<ApiResult<Book>>`.
  - `parseFieldError(message: string): { field: BookField; reason: string } | null`.
- `type ApiResult<T> = { ok: true; data: T } | { ok: false; error: ApiError }`, where `ApiError` is `{ status: number; message: string; kind: ApiErrorKind }`. The 409 distinction is already made in `src/api/`; don't match message texts yourself. `ApiErrorKind` is:
  - 'network': status 0, message 'Could not reach the server.'
  - 'invalid': 400
  - 'not-found': 404
  - 'duplicate-isbn': 409, ISBN taken
  - 'version-conflict': 409, the message starts with `version conflict`
  - 'other': anything else
- The functions never throw.

Router:
- `/books/new` (name `book-new`) renders this view without props: add mode.
- `/books/:id/edit` (name `book-edit`) renders it with the number `id`: edit mode.
- `/books/:id` is named `book`, and `/books` is named `books`.
- App.vue keys the RouterView by `route.path`, so the view is remounted when the path changes.

Test helpers (`@/__tests__/helpers`):
- `makeBook(overrides?: Partial<Book>): Book`, with defaults id 7, isbn '9780132350884', title 'Clean Code', authors ['Robert C. Martin'], version 1 and no optional fields.
- `jsonResponse(status, body)` and `errorResponse(status, message)`.
- `stubFetch(handler: (req: { method: string; url: URL; body: unknown }) => Response | undefined | Promise<...>)` returns the live list of recorded requests, with body as parsed JSON. A handler returning undefined gives a 501; a handler that throws makes fetch reject (`throw new TypeError('Failed to fetch')`).
- `renderRoute(path): Promise<{ wrapper, router }>` mounts the whole App with a memory-history router and a fresh Pinia.
- After setValue and submit, `await flushPromises()`. Use `await vi.waitFor(() => expect(...))` where a response still has to be parsed.

Domain (from the story):
- *Book form*: the shared form for adding and revising a book.
- *Version conflict*: the book was revised by someone else since the form was loaded (API 409 on update).
- The backend is the only authority on validation. The form may mark required fields and use number inputs, but it does not copy the S-02 field rules. Every 400 from the API must be shown, wherever it comes from.
- A 400 message has the form `<field>: <reason>`, e.g. `title: must have 1 to 300 characters`. If `<field>` is one of the form's fields (`isbn`, `title`, `authors`, `publishedYear`, `language`, `pages`), the reason is shown at that field. Any other message is shown at the top of the form.
- Optional fields left empty are omitted from the request body. They are not sent as `""`, `0` or `null`.
- A revision always sends the `version` the form was loaded with. The UI never retries with a newer version on its own, because that would overwrite someone else's change.

Modes:
- `id` undefined is add mode: an empty form with one empty author input, heading "New book", submit button "Add book".
- A number is edit mode: heading "Edit book". Fill the form from `getBook(id)` and keep the loaded `version`. Submit button "Save".
- *Cancel* is a RouterLink to `/books` in add mode and to `/books/<id>` in edit mode.

Fields (each input has a `<label for>` and the id given here):
- ISBN (text, `book-isbn`) and Title (text, `book-title`). Mark both required with a visible marker plus `aria-required="true"`.
- Authors: a `<fieldset>` with `<legend>Authors</legend>`, also marked required.
  - One text input per author, with id `book-author-<n>` and label "Author <n>" (1-based).
  - Each input has a *Remove* button with the accessible name "Remove author <n>".
  - An *Add author* button appends an empty input.
  - There is always at least one input: *Remove* is disabled while there is only one. *Add author* is disabled at 20 inputs.
- Published year (`type="number"`, `book-publishedYear`), Language (text, `book-language`) and Pages (`type="number"`, `book-pages`).
- Use `<form novalidate>` and no `required`, `min`, `max`, `maxlength` or `pattern` attributes. The browser never blocks a submit; the API decides.

Request body:
- `isbn`, `title` and `authors` as typed. Don't trim or normalize; the API does.
- Send every author input, in order. An empty one is sent too, and the API's 400 is shown at Authors.
- Send `publishedYear`, `language` and `pages` only when not empty (whitespace-only counts as empty). Convert the numbers with `Number()`. Vue's `v-model` on a number input yields a number, or `''` when empty.
- Edit mode adds `version`, as loaded.
- Add calls `createBook`; edit calls `updateBook(id, body)`.
- On success: `router.push({ name: 'book', params: { id: book.id } })`.
- While saving, the submit button is disabled and the handler ignores a second submit (guard with a flag).
- What the user typed is kept on every error. Each submit clears the previous errors.

Errors:
- 400 (kind 'invalid'): call `parseFieldError(message)`.
  - With a field: show the reason below that field in an element with id `book-<field>-error` (`book-authors-error` inside the fieldset). The input gets `aria-invalid="true"` and `aria-describedby="book-<field>-error"`. For authors, that applies to the fieldset and to every author input.
  - Without a field: show the message at the top of the form in a `role="alert"` element.
- 409 'duplicate-isbn' (add and edit): "A book with this ISBN already exists" at the ISBN field, linked the same way.
- 409 'version-conflict' (edit):
  - At the top, with role="alert": "This book was changed by someone else." and a sentence saying that *Load latest* replaces the form with the current book and discards the changes.
  - The input stays until the user clicks *Load latest*. That button calls `getBook(id)`, then refills the form, replaces the version and clears all errors.
  - Never resubmit on your own.
- 404:
  - While loading in edit mode: a heading "Book not found" and a RouterLink to `/books`, with no form.
  - On save: "This book no longer exists." at the top, with a link to `/books`.
- Anything else (network, 500, 413, 415, 429): the error message at the top (role="alert"), with the input kept.
- A load error other than 404: role="alert" with the message and a *Retry* button.

Tests: mount with `renderRoute(...)`. Set inputs with `setValue` and submit with `trigger('submit')` on the form. Each acceptance criterion gets at least one test.

Add:
- When I submit the form with ISBN `978-0-13-235088-4`, title, two authors and no optional fields, then `createBook` gets `{isbn, title, authors}` without `publishedYear`, `language` or `pages`, and I land on the new book's details page, which shows the ISBN as `9780132350884`.
- Given the API answers 400 `title: must have 1 to 300 characters`, then that reason is shown at the title field, and what I typed is kept.
- Given the API answers 400 with a message that names no form field, then it is shown at the top of the form.
- Given the API answers 409 (duplicate ISBN), then "A book with this ISBN already exists" is shown at the ISBN field.
- *Add author* adds an input, *Remove* removes one. The last input can't be removed, and *Add author* is disabled at 20 authors.

Revise:
- Given book 7 at version 3, when I open `/books/7/edit`, change the title and save, then `updateBook` gets all editable fields plus `version: 3`, and I land on the details page showing version 4.
- Given the API answers 409 version conflict, then I see "This book was changed by someone else", my input is kept, and a *Load latest* action reloads the form with the current book and version (discarding my changes, after I click it).
- Given the API answers 409 duplicate ISBN, then it is shown at the ISBN field, as when adding.
- Given no book 999, when I open `/books/999/edit`, then I see "Book not found".

Notes on these tests:
- The details page is built in parallel (S04-04). For "I land on the details page", assert the route here:
  - `/books/42` after createBook answers `makeBook({ id: 42, isbn: '9780132350884', ... })`;
  - `/books/7` after updateBook answers version 4.
  S04-06 later checks what the details page shows.
- Still answer `GET /api/books/42` and `GET /api/books/7` (with version 4 after the PUT) in the stub, so the tests keep passing once the real details page is merged.
- Assert the exact add body: `toEqual({ isbn: '978-0-13-235088-4', title, authors: [a, b] })`.
- For revise, use book 7 with all optional fields set and expect `{ isbn, title: <new>, authors, publishedYear, language, pages, version: 3 }`.
- After *Load latest*, a save sends the newly loaded version.

Also test:
- A 400 on an optional field (e.g. `pages: must be between 1 and 10000`) is shown at that field, and `aria-describedby` points to the error element.
- A 400 `authors: each author name must have 1 to 200 characters` is shown at Authors.
- A network error and a 500 are shown at the top, with the input kept.
- Two quick submits send one request.
- Clearing an optional field in edit mode leaves it out of the body.
- A 404 on save shows "This book no longer exists."

title: Add cross-screen flow tests and accessibility checks
prompt:
Story S-04 builds the Vue 3 + TypeScript web UI for the book catalog in `frontend/`. It is a client of the existing `/api/books` endpoints of the `catalog` bounded context and uses its language: a *book* is *added* to the *catalog*, *revised* and *removed*. The backend and `backend/api/openapi.yaml` don't change.

Rules for every frontend task:
- Gate: `cd frontend && npm run typecheck && npm test` must pass; run both before you finish. `src/api/schema.d.ts` is generated and must never be edited.
- You can't run `npm install`, so add no dependencies.
- No `any` (use `unknown` and narrow) and no `v-html` anywhere in `src/`; a guard test fails on either.
- Tests mock the API only at the `fetch` boundary.

These tasks are merged:
- S04-03: the catalog page, `views/BookListView.vue`.
- S04-04: the details screen with delete, `views/BookDetailView.vue`.
- S04-05: the book form, `views/BookFormView.vue`.

Each of them tested its own screen. This task adds the tests that span screens, which none of them could write, plus the accessibility checks.
- Write `src/__tests__/flows.spec.ts` and `src/__tests__/a11y.spec.ts`.
- You may add helpers to `src/__tests__/helpers.ts` without changing existing signatures.
- If a test reveals a bug in a view or component, fix it minimally in `src/views/` or `src/components/`, and in that screen's tests if they asserted the bug. Say so in your final message. Never weaken a test to make it pass.
- Read the views and components first, to learn their real texts, labels and ids.

Contracts:
- `@/api` provides `listBooks`, `getBook`, `createBook`, `updateBook`, `deleteBook` and `parseFieldError`.
  - They return `ApiResult<T> = { ok: true; data } | { ok: false; error: { status, message, kind } }`.
  - A 409 whose message starts with `version conflict` is kind 'version-conflict'; any other 409 is 'duplicate-isbn'.
- Routes:
  - `/` redirects to `/books`.
  - `/books` is named `books`, `/books/new` is `book-new`, `/books/:id` is `book` and `/books/:id/edit` is `book-edit`.
  - Anything else shows "Page not found" with a link to `/books`.
- Notice: `useNoticeStore` (`@/stores/notice`). App.vue renders it in `role="status"` and clears it after each navigation.
- Helpers (`@/__tests__/helpers`):
  - `makeBook(overrides?)`, `jsonResponse(status, body)`, `errorResponse(status, message)` and `noContent()`.
  - `stubFetch(handler: (req: { method, url: URL, body }) => Response | undefined | Promise<...>)` returns the recorded requests. Undefined gives a 501; a throw makes fetch reject.
  - `renderRoute(path): Promise<{ wrapper, router }>` mounts the whole App with a memory-history router.
  - Use `await flushPromises()` and `await vi.waitFor(...)`.

Flows (`flows.spec.ts`): mount the full App with `renderRoute`. Behind `stubFetch`, put a small in-memory fake catalog:
- GET list, honoring author, offset and limit and returning the total.
- GET one; 404 for unknown ids.
- POST: assign the next id and normalize the ISBN by removing hyphens and spaces.
- PUT: check the version, answering 409 `version conflict: the book was changed since it was read` on a mismatch, and increment it.
- DELETE: 204, or 404 for unknown ids.

Cover these acceptance criteria end to end. They are quoted from the story:
- Add: "When I submit the form with ISBN `978-0-13-235088-4`, title, two authors and no optional fields, then `createBook` gets `{isbn, title, authors}` without `publishedYear`, `language` or `pages`, and I land on the new book's details page, which shows the ISBN as `9780132350884`." Also check that the unset optional fields show "—" there.
- Revise: "Given book 7 at version 3, when I open `/books/7/edit`, change the title and save, then `updateBook` gets all editable fields plus `version: 3`, and I land on the details page showing version 4." Also check that the new title is shown.
- Remove: "Given book 7, when I click Delete, then a confirmation naming its title appears. Cancel closes it without calling the API. Delete calls `deleteBook` and returns to `/books` with a 'Deleted <title>' notice." Start on the catalog page and open the book through its title link. Delete it, then check that:
  - the notice is shown on the catalog page;
  - the book is no longer listed;
  - the notice is gone after the next navigation.
- "Given the book was already removed (404 on delete), then I also return to `/books`. The book is gone either way."
- Navigation:
  - *New book* on the catalog page opens the empty form, and the form's *Cancel* returns to `/books`.
  - The header link leads to `/books`.
  - `/` lands on `/books`.
  - An unknown path shows "Page not found" with a link to `/books`.

Accessibility (`a11y.spec.ts`), for the criterion "Every input has a `<label>`, and a field's error is linked to it with `aria-describedby`":
- On `/books`, `/books/new` and `/books/7/edit` (book 7 with all optional fields and three authors):
  - Every `input`, `select` and `textarea` has a non-empty label: a `<label for>` matching its id, or a wrapping `<label>`.
  - Ids are unique on the page.
  - Every button has an accessible name (text or `aria-label`).
- In add and edit mode, for each form field (`isbn`, `title`, `authors`, `publishedYear`, `language`, `pages`), a 400 `<field>: some reason` gives that field's input or inputs:
  - `aria-invalid="true"`;
  - an `aria-describedby` whose ids all exist and whose text contains the reason.
- The same holds for the 409 duplicate ISBN at the ISBN field.
- A 400 that names no field appears in a `role="alert"` element.

title: Document the frontend and rewrite frontend/README.md
prompt:
Story S-04 added a Vue 3 + TypeScript web UI for the book catalog in `frontend/`: a catalog page, book details with delete, and a book form for adding and revising. It is a client of the `catalog` API.

Write `docs/frontend.md` and rewrite the scaffold's `frontend/README.md`. Change nothing else, and no code.

Document what exists, not what was planned. Read:
- `frontend/src/**`: router, views, components, `src/api/`, `src/stores/notice.ts`, `src/__tests__/helpers.ts`.
- `frontend/package.json`, `frontend/vite.config.ts` and `frontend/vitest.config.ts`.
- The root `Makefile` and `backend/api/openapi.yaml`.
Check every command, route, file name and UI text against them.

`docs/frontend.md` should be concise and skimmable, with these sections:

1. Overview
   - What the UI is for: a librarian browses, adds, revises and removes books.
   - The stack: Vue 3, TypeScript, Vue Router, Pinia (only for the flash notice), openapi-fetch, Vitest + @vue/test-utils.
   - The domain terms the UI uses: *book*, *ISBN* (shown normalized, as the API returns it), *version*, *catalog page*, *book form*, *version conflict*.

2. Running it
   - `make mongo`.
   - `make backend`: the API on :8000. `SEED_DEMO_DATA=true make backend` seeds the demo books.
   - `make frontend`: Vite on http://localhost:5173, proxying `/api` to :8000.
   - Run `npm install` once in `frontend/`. Take the Node version from `engines`.

3. Screens and routes
   - A table with the route, the screen and the API operations it uses (`listBooks`, `getBook`, `createBook`, `updateBook`, `deleteBook`). Include `/` → `/books` and "Page not found".
   - The list state in the URL (`/books?author=...&offset=...`), 20 books per page.

4. How the UI maps to the API
   - The one typed client in `src/api/`, with `ApiResult` and `ApiError` (`{status, message, kind}`).
   - Types are generated from `backend/api/openapi.yaml` into the gitignored `src/api/schema.d.ts` by `npm run generate`, which also runs before `dev` and `type-check`.
   - After a spec change, run `npm run typecheck` and fix what no longer compiles.
   - No hand-written API types, and no `fetch` outside `src/api/`. Requests go to the page's own origin.

5. How errors are shown
   - A table:
     - a 400 naming a form field: at that field, linked with `aria-describedby`;
     - any other 400: top of the form;
     - a 409 duplicate ISBN: at the ISBN field;
     - a 409 version conflict (the message starts with `version conflict`): a banner with *Load latest*, never an automatic retry;
     - a 404: "Book not found";
     - network errors and 5xx: the message with *Retry*.
   - Then the rules:
     - The backend is the only authority on validation.
     - Empty optional fields are left out of the request body.
     - A revision sends the version the form was loaded with.
     - Delete asks for confirmation in the page and ends with the "Deleted <title>" notice.

6. Tests
   - `npm run typecheck && npm test` is the frontend gate.
   - The API is mocked at `fetch` with `src/__tests__/helpers.ts` (`stubFetch`, `renderRoute`, `makeBook`, ...).
   - The guard test (no `any`, no `v-html`), the flow tests and the accessibility tests.
   - Tests live in `__tests__/` folders.

7. A short tree of `frontend/src/`.

8. Not done yet: serving the built app in production and in docker-compose (a follow-up story), browser end-to-end tests, i18n.

`frontend/README.md`: replace the Vite template text with a short README:
- what the app is;
- the commands: `npm install`, `npm run dev` (or `make frontend` from the repo root), `npm run generate`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run lint`;
- a link to `../docs/frontend.md` for everything else.

title: Security review of the books frontend
prompt: Story S-04 added a Vue 3 + TypeScript UI for the book catalog in `frontend/`: - a catalog page with an author filter and paging in the URL query; - book details with an in-page delete confirmation and a "Deleted " notice; - a book form for adding and revising, which shows API error messages at fields or at the top; - one typed API client in `src/api/`, built on openapi-fetch with types generated from `backend/api/openapi.yaml`; - Vite in dev, proxying `/api` to the Go backend on :8000. Review the frontend's security. The backend is unchanged and was already reviewed (see `docs/security/`); look at it only where the UI depends on it. Authentication and authorization are out of scope: list "no authentication" once as an accepted risk. Deliverables: 1. A report in `docs/security/S04-08-books-frontend.md`, in the format of the existing reports: - scope; - threat model: assets, entry points, trust boundaries and the STRIDE threats that apply; - a findings table with ID, title, severity, location, impact, recommendation and follow-up; - accepted risks; - what you checked and found fine; - manual follow-ups. 2. Frontend security regression tests in `frontend/src/__tests__/security_*.spec.ts`. - Use Vitest + @vue/test-utils with the helpers in `src/__tests__/helpers.ts`: `stubFetch`, `renderRoute`, `makeBook`, `jsonResponse` and `errorResponse`. - Each test pins the secure behavior. If the behavior doesn't hold yet, use `it.skip('SECURITY <id>: fixed by follow-up <proposal title>', ...)`, so the gate stays green. - These replace the Go e2e security tests your role normally writes. Write no Go tests, and don't run backend/check.sh. - The gate here is `cd frontend && npm run typecheck && npm test`. No `any` and no `v-html`: a guard test checks both. 3. Proposals in `.orch-proposals.json`. - Use `role: "frontend"` with the narrowest scopes under `frontend/**`, including the skipped test file to un-skip. - Workers can only Read, Edit and Write, and run `npm test` / `npm run typecheck`. They have no `npm install` and no network. So dependency upgrades, `npm audit` and anything else that needs the registry are marked `manual` in the findings table, with the exact commands under "Manual follow-ups". - Backend and spec changes are out of scope for this story. If the UI needs one (e.g. a machine-readable error code instead of matching `version conflict`), propose it with `role: "api"` or `"backend"` and give the reason. - Rate severity honestly. `medium` proposals are approved automatically and `low` ones are parked. What to look at: - XSS: - `v-html`, `innerHTML`, `:href`/`:src`/`:style` bound to book data or server messages, `javascript:` URLs, runtime template compilation, `eval`/`new Function`. - Book data (title, authors, language, ISBN), API error messages and the notice must render only as text. - Pin this with tests: payloads like `<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>` and `javascript:alert(1)` in titles, authors and API error messages must create no element or attribute. Check the catalog page, the details page, the delete confirmation, the form (field and top-level errors) and the notice. - Link targets: - Every RouterLink and href is built from numeric ids or fixed paths. - There is no open redirect (e.g. a `redirect` or `next` query). - `target="_blank"` appears only with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. - The scaffold's external links are gone. - What reaches the URL: - The author filter (user input) in `/books?author=...` ends up in history, in the Vite and backend access logs, and in Referer headers. - Book titles, error messages and the notice must not reach the URL. - Check that the query parsing (repeated params, huge values, a non-numeric or negative offset) can't break the page or reach the API unencoded. - API client: - Requests stay same-origin (`baseUrl` is the page origin, with no hardcoded hosts). - Error messages are only displayed, never interpreted. - The 409 distinction and the 400 field parsing can't be abused to place text somewhere misleading. - A malformed response (e.g. a 200 with a non-JSON body) gives an error state, not an unhandled rejection or a blank page. - Dev server and build: - In `vite.config.ts`: the `/api` proxy (which paths match, `changeOrigin`, host binding), and whether `vite-plugin-vue-devtools` stays out of production builds. - No secrets in `import.meta.env` or `VITE_*` variables. - Source maps. - Serving the built app in production is a follow-up story. Record what it will need (a CSP for the SPA, `Referrer-Policy`, `frame-ancestors`) as manual notes, not as proposals. - Dependencies, checked offline: - `package.json` ranges versus the exact pins in `package-lock.json`. - The lockfileVersion; that every `resolved` URL is on https://registry.npmjs.org and has an `integrity`; that there are no git, http or file dependencies; packages with `hasInstallScript`; the `overrides` block. - You have no network and can't run `npm audit`. Say which versions you couldn't verify, and list `npm audit` and `npm audit signatures` as manual follow-ups.
